ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The outer frame in the figure is a square wall surface. Inside the wall there are three gray squares: one larger gray square below is upright, located in the middle of the bottom side; on the upper left and upper right there is one gray square of the same size each, both rotated into diamonds. The top vertex of the upper-left diamond is on the upper side of the wall, the left vertex is on the left side of the wall, the right vertex meets the left vertex of the upper-right diamond in the middle, and the bottom vertex falls on the upper-left corner of the lower square. The upper-right diamond is similar; its right vertex is on the right side of the wall, and the bottom vertex falls on the upper-right corner of the lower square. Reasoning: The wall is 16 meters by 16 meters. The two upper small squares form 45° with the wall sides, so in the figure they can be regarded as diamonds with horizontal and vertical diagonals. Let the horizontal diagonal length of each upper diamond be d. The left diamond extends horizontally from the left wall side to the middle contact point, and the right diamond extends from the middle contact point to the right wall side. The two equal horizontal diagonals together equal the wall width 16 meters, so 2d=16, d=8. The area of a square equals half the square of its diagonal, so the area of each upper small square is 8^2/2=32, and the two total 64. The side length of the lower upright square equals the horizontal distance between the bottom vertices of the two diamonds; these two bottom vertices are respectively below the midpoints of the horizontal diagonals of the left and right diamonds, so the distance is 8 meters. Therefore the area of the lower square is 8^2=64. The total gray area B=64+64=128.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the outer wall is a square; the bottom grey square is upright and centered at the bottom; the two equal upper grey squares are diamonds, each with top vertex on the top edge, outer side vertex on the left/right wall, inner vertices touching each other, and bottom vertices forming the two top corners of the bottom square. Read from the text that the wall is 16 m by 16 m and the upper squares are at 45 degrees. Let the horizontal/vertical diagonal of each diamond be d. Since the left diamond spans horizontally from the left wall to the central touching point, and the right diamond spans from that same central point to the right wall, the two equal horizontal diagonals add to the 16 m wall width, so d=8. A square with diagonal d has area d^2/2, so the two upper squares have total area 2*(8^2/2)=64. The bottom square side is the horizontal distance between the lower vertices of the diamonds, which is also 8, so its area is 64. Add the three grey areas to get B=128.

The two smaller grey squares are equal in size and each makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the edge of the wall. The grey squares cover a total area of $B$ metres squared. What is the value of $B$?
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The diagram shows a 16 metre by 16 metre wall. Three grey squares are painted on the wall as shown. The two smaller grey squares are equal in size and each makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the edge of the wall. The grey squares cover a total area of $B$ metres squared. What is the value of $B$?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The outer frame in the figure is a square wall surface. Inside the wall there are three gray squares: one larger gray square below is upright, located in the middle of the bottom side; on the upper left and upper right there is one gray square of the same size each, both rotated into diamonds. The top vertex of the upper-left diamond is on the upper side of the wall, the left vertex is on the left side of the wall, the right vertex meets the left vertex of the upper-right diamond in the middle, and the bottom vertex falls on the upper-left corner of the lower square. The upper-right diamond is similar; its right vertex is on the right side of the wall, and the bottom vertex falls on the upper-right corner of the lower square. Reasoning: The wall is 16 meters by 16 meters. The two upper small squares form 45° with the wall sides, so in the figure they can be regarded as diamonds with horizontal and vertical diagonals. Let the horizontal diagonal length of each upper diamond be d. The left diamond extends horizontally from the left wall side to the middle contact point, and the right diamond extends from the middle contact point to the right wall side. The two equal horizontal diagonals together equal the wall width 16 meters, so 2d=16, d=8. The area of a square equals half the square of its diagonal, so the area of each upper small square is 8^2/2=32, and the two total 64. The side length of the lower upright square equals the horizontal distance between the bottom vertices of the two diamonds; these two bottom vertices are respectively below the midpoints of the horizontal diagonals of the left and right diamonds, so the distance is 8 meters. Therefore the area of the lower square is 8^2=64. The total gray area B=64+64=128.
